final_answer:
Short answer: No on both counts, in all likelihood. Client cannot lawfully stop paying Lessor, and Lessor is not responsible for the defective Trailers. Client's remedy lies against Manufacturer (now in Chapter 7), not Lessor.

1. The Lease is a 'finance lease' under Virginia's UCC Article 2A. Va. Code 8.2A-103(1)(g) defines a finance lease as a lease in which (i) the lessor does not select, manufacture, or supply the goods; (ii) the lessor acquires the goods in connection with the lease; and (iii) one of several conditions is met, including that the lessee receives a copy of the lessor's supply (purchase) contract before signing the lease (with an accurate and complete statement of the supplier's promises and warranties and any disclaimers or limitations of remedy). Here: Client itself picked the model and negotiated refrigeration specs with Manufacturer, so Lessor merely financed (selected nothing, manufactured nothing, supplied nothing); Lessor bought the Trailers from Manufacturer for the Lease; and Client received a complete copy of the purchase agreement, including the two-year warranty, before signing. All elements appear satisfied. The Lease is not a consumer lease (Client is a business), which matters for 8.2A-407.

2. Hell-or-high-water. Under Va. Code 8.2A-407(1)-(2), in a finance lease that is not a consumer lease, the lessee's promises under the lease become irrevocable and independent upon the lessee's acceptance of the goods; the promise is enforceable between the parties and by or against third parties (including assignees) and is not subject to cancellation, termination, modification, repudiation, excuse, or substitution without the consent of the party to whom it runs. The section is self-executing, so the statute would apply even without the Lease's 'absolute and unconditional, irrespective of any defense or setoff' language; the Lease clause independently confirms it. Consequently Client cannot withhold rent, set off or recoup damages from the compressor failures, or treat Manufacturer's bankruptcy as excusing payment. Client has accepted the Trailers (it used them for four months and did not reject), so independence has attached. Non-payment is a default exposing Client to the Lease's default remedies and 8.2A-523 et seq. (accelerated rent or repossession and damages, subject to the Lease terms, plus likely attorney's fees if the Lease provides).

3. Lessor's liability. Va. Code 8.2A-209 gives the finance lessee the benefit of the supplier's promises and warranties (including those in the supply contract), as if the lessee were a party to the supply contract, and the lessor makes no implied warranty of merchantability or fitness in a finance lease (8.2A-212/-213 apply to the lessor only where it is a merchant 'with respect to goods of that kind' and, for finance leases, the implied warranties of 8.2A-212 and -213 are expressly not given by the finance lessor; see the Article 2A scheme). The Lease contains no lessor warranty and directs equipment claims to Manufacturer. So Lessor has no warranty liability, and the defective compressors do not support revocation of acceptance or rescission against Lessor. Client's warranty rights run against Manufacturer; they are now an unsecured claim in the Chapter 7 case (file a proof of claim; recovery likely small). Lessor's purchase-agreement warranty rights travel to Client under 8.2A-209, but are worth only what the estate pays; Client should check whether any extended-warranty, product-liability insurance, or third-party compressor-maker (OEM) warranty, or an assignee/successor manufacturer, applies.

4. Caveats and exceptions. (a) The hell-or-high-water rule does not shield Lessor's own fraud, bad faith, or misrepresentation, or lessor misconduct (e.g., if Lessor made representations about the Trailers' performance, or was in truth involved in selection or supply, which would destroy finance-lease status). (b) Unconscionability under 8.2A-108 is theoretically available but unlikely between commercial parties. (c) Lessor must itself have performed (e.g., delivered the goods). (d) If the Lease were found not to be a finance lease, the clause would still be enforced as a contract term in most courts, but the statutory protection would not apply and implied warranties could arise; on the stated facts, finance-lease status is solid. (e) If Lessor assigned the Lease, the assignee takes free of Client's claims against Manufacturer. (f) I did not verify the text of the Lease against statutory conspicuousness requirements; 8.2A-407 requires none. (g) No Virginia case law was reviewed within budget; statutory text was verified only via search summaries because the official site fetch was blocked.

Practical advice: Client should resume payments (curing arrears) to avoid default, acceleration, repossession and deficiency exposure; assert claims in Manufacturer's bankruptcy; explore negotiated relief with Lessor (it may agree to cooperate, or to work out repairs by a third-party shop, but is not obliged to); consider repairs under any component maker's warranty and mitigation costs.

issues.text: Does the arrangement qualify as a finance lease under Va. Code 8.2A-103(1)(g)?
Does the statutory hell-or-high-water rule (8.2A-407) make Client's rent obligation irrevocable and independent despite defects and Manufacturer's bankruptcy?
Is Lessor liable for warranty or otherwise responsible for the defective Trailers (8.2A-209 and absence of lessor warranties)?
Exceptions: lessor fraud/bad faith, unconscionability, loss of finance-lease status, and Client's remedies against Manufacturer.

authorities.title: Definitions (finance lease)
authorities.proposition: Finance lease: lessor does not select, manufacture or supply goods; acquires goods in connection with lease; lessee receives copy of supply contract before signing lease (or other qualifying condition).

authorities.title: Irrevocable promises: finance leases
authorities.proposition: In a non-consumer finance lease the lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent upon acceptance and are not subject to cancellation, termination, modification, repudiation, excuse, or substitution without consent; self-executing.

authorities.title: Third-party beneficiaries of express and implied warranties (finance lease)
authorities.proposition: Finance lessee gets the benefit of the supplier's promises and warranties; lessor makes no warranty by virtue of being finance lessor.

claims.text: The Lease qualifies as a finance lease because Client selected the Trailers and specs, Lessor only financed, and Client received the full purchase agreement before signing.

Under 8.2A-407 and the Lease clause, Client's payment obligations became irrevocable and independent upon acceptance, so Client cannot withhold or set off for the compressor defects or Manufacturer's bankruptcy.
Lessor is not liable for the defects; Client's warranty rights run against Manufacturer under 8.2A-209 and are an unsecured bankruptcy claim.

unresolved: Official Virginia Code site fetch was blocked; text of 8.2A-407 and 8.2A-103 confirmed only via search summaries, and 8.2A-209 and the implied-warranty sections (8.2A-212/-213) were not directly verified.
No Virginia case law on hell-or-high-water enforcement or lessor bad-faith exceptions was researched.
Whether Lessor made any extra-contractual representations or assigned the Lease is unknown.
